PROJECT NO. 58777


ERCOT’S FINAL RECOMMENDATION OF MODELING ASSUMPTIONS
AND CONE STUDY FOR THE 2026 RELIABILITY ASSESSMENT

Pursuant to 16 Texas Administrative Code (TAC) § 25.508(c)(1)(C), Electric Reliability Council of Texas, Inc. (ERCOT) files this Final Recommendation of Modeling Assumptions and CONE Study for the 2026 Reliability Assessment.  The table of final recommended modeling assumptions is included here as Attachment A.  A new column has been added to indicate any modifications to each assumption.  Additionally, new assumptions or an assumption that was split into two separate assumptions are included in additional rows, which use red font.
This recommendation is timely filed by March 23, 2026, in accordance with the timeline recommended by Public Utility Commission of Texas (Commission) Staff for performance of the 2026 Reliability Assessment.
Reliability Assessment Development Process
Under the process established in 16 TAC § 25.508(c), on January 15, 2026, ERCOT filed a comprehensive list of initial proposed modeling assumptions to be used in the Reliability Assessment.  As explained in that filing, ERCOT will conduct the assessment using PowerGem, LLC’s (PowerGem) Strategic Energy & Risk Valuation Model (SERVM), which is a probability-based model simulation of the ERCOT System commonly used in the industry.
ERCOT also filed a proposal to update the Cost of New Entry (CONE) value.  Although CONE is not a modeling input for SERVM, the value used for CONE will inform any recommendation of market design changes for the ERCOT Region should the Reliability Assessment find that the reliability standard is not being met currently in 2026 or is not anticipated to be met in 2029.  Because the most recent CONE value to be used for planning purposes was determined in 2024 and there continue to be rapid changes in the electric power sector since that study was performed, ERCOT proposed that The Brattle Group (Brattle) and its subcontractor, Sargent & Lundy (S&L), be engaged to perform a CONE update study on an expedited basis for use in the Reliability Assessment process.
In accordance with 16 TAC § 25.508(c)(1)(B), Commission Staff filed Questions for Comment to solicit stakeholder feedback on the initial proposed modeling inputs and on the proposal to update CONE.  By March 3, 2026, 15 stakeholders and the Independent Market Monitor (IMM) filed comments addressing Commission Staff’s questions.
ERCOT has reviewed stakeholders’ filed comments to evaluate whether any changes should be made to ERCOT’s initial proposed modeling assumptions or its CONE study proposal.  Pursuant to 16 TAC § 25.508(c)(1)(C), ERCOT has consulted with Commission Staff in the development of ERCOT’s final recommendation.  Based on the timeline filed by Commission Staff, ERCOT understands that Commission Staff may file a separate recommendation and the Commission will then consider approving a set of modeling assumptions at the April 17, 2026, Open Meeting.  Upon approval of the modeling assumptions, ERCOT will work with PowerGem to begin running the model simulations using those inputs to conduct the Reliability Assessment of the ERCOT System.
Final Recommendation of Modeling Assumptions
After reviewing stakeholder’s filed comments and consulting with Commission Staff, ERCOT proposes the following updates in its recommended modeling assumptions, which are included in the updated Attachment A.  First, in regard to modeling the resource mix for 2026 and 2029, ERCOT continues to recommend that the resource portfolio use the data from the December 2025 Capacity, Demand, and Reserves (CDR) Report, but with an update to reflect any resources that experienced at least a 100 megawatt (MW) increase or decrease in capacity since the publication of that report.  In addition to ensuring that the most current resource values are used, this will result in certain Texas Energy Fund (TEF) projects being included that have now reached the threshold under which they would be included in a CDR.  Note that several stakeholders filed comments recommending that TEF projects be better incorporated into the generation portfolio, including Advanced Power Alliance (APA) and American Clean Power Association (ACPA), Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA), Texas Competitive Power Advocates (TCPA), and Texas Solar + Storage Association (TSSA).
Second, in regard to modeling Dispatchable Reliability Reserve Service (DRRS), ERCOT continues to recommend including it in modeling for 2029, however the Ancillary Service Demand Curve (ASDC) should be updated to reflect the IMM’s and ERCOT’s joint proposal from the March 9, 2026, Technical Advisory Committee DRRS Workshop No. 3 to improve the curve.  Shell Energy North America (US) LP’s comments recommended additional efforts to examine adjustments to ASDCs to support evaluation of market design options.
Third, in regard to modeling scarcity pricing, ERCOT previously indicated that it was investigating with PowerGem if and how the Emergency Pricing Program (EPP) can be implemented in SERVM.  Lower Colorado River Authority (LCRA) recommended that the EPP logic be incorporated in order to more precisely discount scarcity pricing during a modeled shortage event.  ERCOT and PowerGem have determined that the EPP can be incorporated into SERVM’s scarcity pricing modeling.
Fourth, ERCOT recommends that net metering load arrangements that involve Large Loads co-located with an existing Generation Resource be modeled in SERVM based on the operational conditions approved by the Commission for each such arrangement. 
Fifth, given that certain Large Load curtailment mechanisms remain under development, ERCOT recommends that the current practice be maintained of applying overall curtailment percentages to aggregate forecasted Large Loads by industry type.  The curtailment percentages used would be from the upcoming 2026 Large Load RFI results, which are anticipated to be received by April 1, 2026.
Finally, ERCOT recommends that the most up-to-date load forecast be used to perform the Reliability Assessment, which will be the 2026 Regional Transmission Plan (RTP) Compliance Plan load forecast that is developed this spring.  As noted in ERCOT’s prior initial recommendation, the 2026 RTP Compliance Plan load forecast will be developed based on load forecast data scheduled to be provided by the Transmission Service Providers (TSPs) to ERCOT on April 1, 2026 and therefore that load forecast could be ready in April or May 2026.  Use of the load forecast developed with this data would ensure that the Reliability Assessment Report is based on the same load forecast data used for other planning purposes but will result in a delayed delivery of the report of at least one month (i.e., mid-to-late September 2026) and potentially longer depending on the quality and timing of the data received.
Updates to Cost of New Entry Study Recommendation
Although there were a handful of exceptions, most stakeholders that filed comments in response to Commission Staff’s Question No. 1 were in favor of updating the CONE value for use in the Reliability Assessment.  ERCOT continues to recommend that an expedited CONE update study be performed in order to develop a refreshed CONE value to use for the Reliability Assessment and other planning-related purposes.  In order to ensure that an updated CONE value can be timely delivered, ERCOT has engaged Brattle and its subcontractor, S&L, to perform an expedited CONE study and they have now begun the study process.  If the Commission provides guidance related to a CONE study at the April 17, 2026, Open Meeting, Brattle and S&L can adjust the study approach at that point to reflect such guidance without having a significant impact on the timing of deliverability of the refreshed CONE value, so long as the primary reference technology is either a frame combustion turbine (CT) or an internal combustion engine (ICE) and there is not more than one alternative reference technology.
For the primary reference technology, Brattle recommended evaluating either a small frame combustion turbine (CT) or an internal combustion engine (ICE).  Both of these are gas-fired, quick-start generation that are anticipated to be available for development in the ERCOT Region by 2029.  ERCOT recommends that a small frame CT is the more appropriate reference technology for the ERCOT Region due to concerns that ICEs have more risk to their availability given data centers’ substantial acquisitions of that technology, while small frame CTs are likely to have greater availability for development.  This would also be consistent with the reference technology used to determine the current CONE planning value of $140 per kilowatt year (kW-year), which was a frame CT.
If the Commission desires to have an alternative reference technology for consideration in addition to a thermal technology, ERCOT recommends using a solar photovoltaic (PV) plus battery energy storage system (BESS) for the alternative.  The PV+BESS generation type is commonly developed in the ERCOT Region, is anticipated to continue to be available for development by 2029, and study of this type as the alternative reference technology would also be consistent with the alternative reference technology evaluated in the 2024 CONE Study.
To avoid potential delays in the delivery of the CONE study results, ERCOT would recommend limiting the CONE study to evaluation of no more than a primary and alternative reference technology.  If three or more reference technologies are studied, this could delay the conclusion of the study.
Conclusion
ERCOT appreciates the opportunity to recommend these modeling assumptions and a CONE Study approach for the Commission’s consideration.  ERCOT stands ready to provide any additional information that may be helpful.  ERCOT personnel will be available for questions at the Commission’s Open Meeting on April 17, 2026.



Dated: March 23, 2026

Respectfully submitted,
